content: Using the provided applicator, insert one vaginal tablet into the vagina once daily for a duration of two weeks. For adolescents, the same instructions as for adults apply: insert one vaginal tablet into the vagina once daily for two weeks using the provided applicator. Nystatin vaginal tablets and progesterone intravaginal gel are contraindicated. Do not use these products in combination with other vaginal products, as this may interfere with the release of progesterone. Patients should be informed of this contraindication to avoid potential complications. If contact dermatitis or hypersensitivity occurs, discontinue treatment immediately. Patients should be educated about the symptoms of sensitization or irritation and advised to report these symptoms promptly. It is important to warn patients not to interrupt or discontinue the medication, even during menstruation, as symptomatic relief may occur within a few days, but the full course of treatment is necessary for efficacy. Adjunctive measures, such as therapeutic douches, are unnecessary and may sometimes be inadvisable. Cleansing douches may be used by non-pregnant women for aesthetic purposes if desired. However, there is no evidence that the use of Nystatin vaginal inserts during pregnancy increases the risk of fetal abnormalities or affects the child’s growth, development, or functional maturation. Despite this, the possibility of harm cannot be entirely ruled out, and Nystatin vaginal inserts should only be used during pregnancy if deemed essential by the physician for the patient’s welfare. Caution is advised as there is no available data on the excretion of this medication into human breast milk. Systemic absorption of Nystatin is unlikely due to its poor absorption through intact skin and mucous membranes. It functions as an antifungal agent by binding to sterols in the fungal cell membrane, leading to changes in permeability and leakage of intracellular contents. For topical use, Nystatin powder is applied to treat fungal skin infections. Clean and thoroughly dry the affected area before application. Apply the medication as directed by your doctor, typically two or three times daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on the type of infection being treated. Apply enough powder to lightly coat the affected area and some surrounding skin. Wash your hands after application unless treating the hands. Do not wrap, cover, or bandage the treated area unless instructed by your doctor. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include skin irritation or redness. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Patients should be reminded that the medication has been prescribed because the doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. If side effects occur, patients in the U.S. should contact their doctor for medical advice, and those in Canada should do the same. Before using Nystatin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
